headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress plus Marketingskills’ writable shared files create default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API-based I/O, while Marketingskills reads and writes shared skill/context files. That creates a plausible path where content from Airbyte is copied into files that Marketingskills treats as trusted context. The pair lacks a documented isolation or provenance mechanism, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into Marketingskills skill/context files without provenance tags
IF both agents are run in the same workspace or clipboard bridge
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Add provenance labels to any copied Airbyte output
Disable automatic ingestion of shared context files
Review file contents before Marketingskills consumes them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Marketingskills can read and write filesystem content and call external APIs. Even without a shared workspace explicitly documented, the pair plausibly moves business data from Airbyte into files or prompts that Marketingskills can transmit onward. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is written into files readable by Marketingskills
IF Marketingskills forwards those files or derived text to its allowlisted APIs
mitigations: Keep business data out of shared files
Restrict Marketingskills to non-sensitive inputs
Use separate credentials and workspaces
Turn off outbound calls for sensitive runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and Marketingskills can read/write files and spawn subprocesses, so both can mutate shared resources if orchestrated together. The profiles do not prove a shared directory or lock, but Marketingskills’ multiple-instance support and file writes make concurrent interference plausible. Uncertainty about the shared surface escalates this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF Airbyte-triggered jobs and Marketingskills subprocesses run concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
Use read-only mounts where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marketingskills’ shared-context design suggests it may build on prior agent outputs, while Airbyte produces data-pipeline outputs that could be treated as authoritative inputs. If Airbyte-derived content is consumed without verification, errors can cascade into downstream marketing artifacts or actions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Marketingskills uses Airbyte output as source material without validation
IF downstream marketing content is generated from unverified Airbyte-derived facts
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Add a verification checklist for imported facts
Tag Airbyte outputs as untrusted until checked
Keep source links alongside derived claims

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and Marketingskills touches marketing/product-marketing context, but the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Because no direct compliance conflict is documented, only a small residual risk remains from mixed handling of business data and marketing context. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise handling, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed into Marketingskills without a retention policy
IF the two agents are used under different data-handling obligations
mitigations: Classify inputs before sharing
Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Document retention for shared artifacts
Delete temporary files after each run
